Filing this issue to keep track of when the team that owns it releases an update that does support .NET Core.\r\n\r\nReference: https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.AlwaysEncrypted.AzureKeyVaultProvider\r\n",

      "body": "Any update on this? or any timeline for this to be included in .NET Core?"

      "body": "> Any update on this? or any timeline for this to be included in .NET Core?\r\n\r\nNo update. It's not \"in .NET Core\". It's an independent library which needs to support .NET Core targets. The team that owns it says it's a high priority on their TODO list but there is no timeline right now."
    },
    {
      "id": 524003369,
      "url": "https://github.com/dotnet/SqlClient/issues/111#issuecomment-524003369",
      "created_at": "2019-08-22T17:35:09Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "I was able to get this to work by re-implementing the `SqlColumnEncryptionAzureKeyVaultProvider` by mostly copying the decompiled source of the .NET Framework version. Using dotPeek or ILSpy on the dll inside the https://www.nuget.org/api/v2/package/Microsoft.SqlServer.Management.AlwaysEncrypted.AzureKeyVaultProvider/2.1.0 nupkg you can see the decompiled source of `SqlColumnEncryptionAzureKeyVaultProvider`, and the only real things that needed changing that I could see were replacing `new SHA256Cng()` with `SHA256.Create()` a few times and replacing `System.Data.SqlClient` with `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient` (and I was lazy and replaced the resource managed strings in Strings.cs with constants).\r\nThen, with this copied class, the only nuget packages you need (which are .net standard) are `Microsoft.Azure.KeyVault` and `Microsoft.IdentityModel.Clients.ActiveDirectory`. From there, I was able to follow this guide https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sql-database/sql-database-always-encrypted-azure-key-vault#register-the-azure-key-vault-provider without issue. \r\n\r\nMy test application had these package references:\r\n```\r\n<PackageReference Include=\"Microsoft.Azure.KeyVault\" Version=\"2.3.2\" />\r\n<PackageReference Include=\"Microsoft.Data.SqlClient\" Version=\"1.0.19221.1-Preview\" />\r\n<PackageReference Include=\"Microsoft.IdentityModel.Clients.ActiveDirectory\" Version=\"5.2.0\" />\r\n```\r\nAlso tested and worked (on my machine! through windows and docker) with Microsoft.Azure.KeyVault 3.0.4.\r\n\r\nI would post the source of the provider, but I'm not sure if posting modified decompiled source goes against the license. "
    },
    {

      "body": "Update: The team that owns the AKV provider is going to pass it to us (the SqlClient team) to work on. We will start working on it as soon as we can and hopefully have an updated version out in September/October."

Thanks!"

      "body": "Any update or timeframe on this? \r\n\r\nWe have several new .Net Core projects running on Azure app service that have to use (time consuming and not ideally performing) work arounds to handle the encrypted data via the regular EF Azure KeyVault provider. \r\n\r\nI tried @dferretti suggestion but could not get it to work in the limited time frame I was given.\r\n\r\nThank you!"

      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 8",
      "body": "@cperras @Tim-Bijnens @beufordy3k @naresh1990 @dferretti \r\n\r\nWe have released the first public preview version of Azure Key Vault Provider today, please download from here: [v1.0.0-preview1](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.AlwaysEncrypted.AzureKeyVaultProvider)\r\n\r\nPlease note that the AKV Provider is targeted for **SqlClient v1.1** hence will work with [v1.1.0-preview1](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Data.SqlClient/1.1.0-preview1.19275.1) version of Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.\r\n\r\nPlease try it out and send us your feedback so we can enhance the library for a stable version."
